transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, my family told me I needed to come see you. I... I just keep telling them that I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back, and I had these ugly thoughts sometimes, so it's my fault. And now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at my church because of me. I just... that's why I'm here.
How long have you been having these thoughts about being responsible for your friend's death and the Lord punishing your church?
It's been about two months now. Ever since my close friend passed away... that's when all this started.
Besides these guilty thoughts since your friend passed away, have you been feeling persistently sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day for these two months?

I don't know if I'd call it sad, exactly. Or empty. I just... I mostly just think about what I did. That's what sits with me all day, just knowing I brought this on everyone. I haven't really noticed feeling empty, just... guilty, I guess.
Over these past two months, have there been days when you felt sad or down, even if you weren't thinking about the guilt?
No, I... I don't think so. There really aren't any times when I'm not thinking about the guilt. It's just always on my mind. So, no, I can't say I've just felt sad outside of all that.
When you think about your friend's death and what happened at church, do you also feel sad or down in your mood, or is it mainly just the guilty thoughts without that sad feeling?

I think it's mainly just the guilty thoughts. I don't really feel sad, like... like I want to cry or anything. It's just this heavy feeling of knowing I'm to blame for what happened. So, no, I wouldn't really call it a sad mood. It's just the guilt.
When you say the Lord is punishing your church because of you, do you truly believe that is happening, or is it more of a fear you have?

No, I... I know it is happening. It's not just a fear. When I'm sitting there and the pastor says the prayers, or when the choir sings certain lines... I know they are really warning me. They're letting me know that God has marked me, and that the whole church is suffering because I brought this on us. I just know it's the truth.

If I told you that the pastor and choir members have said they were NOT specifically warning you or sending you messages, would you be able to consider that possibility, or are you completely certain they are communicating with you?

I hear what you're saying, but... I just know what I hear. When the pastor is up there saying the prayers, or the choir is singing those specific lines, they are warning me. It's not something I'm guessing at. They are telling me that God has marked me, and that our church is suffering because of what I did. So, even if they told you they weren't... I know they are.
Before your friend died two months ago, did you ever have these kinds of beliefs where you could tell that people were sending you hidden messages or warning you about something?

No, I never had thoughts like that before. Before my friend died, I never believed the choir or the pastor were sending me warnings. I just went to service like anyone else. 

All of this... it really only started after she passed and I sank into this state. It's just been these past few weeks, after I got so low and the guilt got so heavy, that I started hearing the messages. But before that? No, never.

When you first started having the guilty thoughts about your friend's death two months ago, did those guilt thoughts come before you started hearing the messages from the pastor and choir, or did they start around the same time?

The guilt definitely came first. When she passed away two months ago, that's when I started feeling so awful, just blaming myself and sinking really low. It was only after I got into that dark place, maybe just in the past few weeks, that I started hearing the messages at church. Like I said before, I never had thoughts about the pastor or choir warning me before she died. It all started after the guilt got so heavy.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F23 (Brief Psychotic Disorder). The patient's psychotic features (delusions of reference regarding pastor/choir messages, delusion of guilt about friend's death and church punishment) emerged AFTER and secondary to severe depressive symptoms (guilt, low mood, sinking into 'dark place'). This is mood-congruent psychosis occurring within Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (F32.2), not a primary psychotic disorder. The temporal sequence is clear: guilt and depression first (2 months ago), then psychotic features emerged later (past few weeks) as depression deepened.
